title: Writing / Style / Emoji
slide_intent: Use emoji selectively and by channel so their attention value is preserved and the message remains clear.
strategic_value: Channel-specific guidance can help Duolingo use a playful cue without making every notification equally noisy.
demonstration: The long right panel divides guidance into push notifications, email subject lines and social media, with screenshots illustrating each.
practical_value: Choose placement and frequency for the channel and test subject lines rather than assuming emoji always help.

content_islands.name: Guidance column
content_islands.spec: Place the Emoji heading and attention-versus-restraint rationale at left.

content_islands.name: Worked examples
content_islands.spec: Stack push rules and three notifications, email rules and subject lines, then social guidance and a tweet screenshot.

reference_purposes.Intent: The introductory note says emoji convey information and attract attention but should be used sparingly.
reference_purposes.Expression: The notification, email and social examples show playful emoji in actual communications.
reference_purposes.Application: The page gives channel-specific placement and testing instructions.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Push guidance usually limits a message to one emoji, allows justified exceptions and omits emoji about half the time; email uses emoji then a space before copy, while social rules are looser.

ingredient.name: Channel-specific emoji
ingredient.role: Add a selective cue that draws attention.
ingredient.application: For pushes, usually use one emoji at either end of title or body and omit it about half the time; use justified exceptions. Start emoji-bearing email subjects with emoji plus space and A/B test. Adapt social use to the message.
ingredient.scope: Historical official guidelines from the 2024–2025 archived snapshot; this records the displayed guidance, not current Duolingo product behavior.
